analysis.title: Investor Positioning and Flows - Ready For The Next V-Turn: Moving Tech from Overweight To Neutral
key_insights: DB strategists move Tech (mega-cap growth plus Tech) from overweight to neutral tactically. The rotation into Tech that began late July is the 5th in two years and is near the top of its long-run trend channel.

Risk-reward in Tech is unfavorable near term: about 4pp of outperformance remains to reach the top of the channel versus potentially 16pp of relative downside if the pattern of rotations near channel edges holds. Prior rotations were inverted V-turns.

Positioning in Tech has begun to slip but is still overweight, while most other sectors are neutral or underweight after a slew of negative catalysts. Discretionary positioning is modestly underweight and small caps are underweight.

DB expects Q3 Tech earnings growth of about 55% yoy but thinks it will not be enough near term, because concerns are now centered on future profitability. Ex-Tech growth is forecast at 21% yoy versus 23% in Q2, and median S&P 500 company growth in the mid-teens.
The bar for non-Tech sectors is low because of a prevalent belief there is hardly any growth, so a rotation into other sectors and small caps should ease market breadth concerns.

DB asks whether the Tech rotation reversal will come with a broader selloff. Recent history says yes, but this is colored by rotations that melded into large exogenous shocks such as Liberation Day and the start of the Iran war.
A rotation away from Tech favors cyclical regions: Europe (Tech exposure 9%) over the US (40%) or Asia (30%).
The longer-run Tech outperformance trend is intact: Tech has beaten the rest of the S&P 500 by 14pp annually over the last decade on much stronger earnings growth.

Aggregate equity positioning edged lower but remains modestly overweight (0.23sd, 56th percentile). Discretionary positioning (-0.23sd, 32nd percentile) is modestly underweight, systematic positioning (0.79sd, 85th percentile) is overweight.

Sector positioning: MCG & Tech fell to 0.42sd (58th percentile), Consumer Cyclicals rose to 0.20sd (80th percentile), Financials fell to -0.55sd (17th percentile), Energy -0.13sd, Industrial Cyclicals -0.29sd, Materials -0.33sd, Real Estate -0.28sd. Defensives are slightly underweight.

Vol control funds' equity allocation is at the 99th percentile. Their sensitivity to selloffs fell materially, which eases deleveraging risk under modest drawdowns, but capacity to add equity is limited.

CTA equity positioning fell materially but remains elevated (67th percentile). Further increases depend more on declining volatility than stronger trend signals. CTA bond shorts are extreme (US 14th, Europe 13th percentile), dollar longs very elevated (97th), gold short (17th), copper (97th) and oil (77th) strongly long.
Risk parity equity allocations rose (77th percentile), reversing last week's derisking. Commodity (97th), REIT (89th) and inflation hedge (85th) exposures remain elevated.

Fund flows: equity funds took in $12.4bn, bond funds $33.8bn (four-month high), and money market funds $166.4bn, the biggest inflow since April 2020. Tech sector funds took in $3.5bn for a second week while Financials had $3.0bn of outflows, the biggest in seven months.

Sentiment and options: the AAII bull-bear spread turned slightly bullish for the first time in five weeks (39th percentile), the call/put volume ratio dipped but is at the 80th percentile, and S&P 500 3m skew rose. Net call volume (5d ma) is at the 99th percentile.

sector_views.rationale: Moved from overweight to neutral tactically. Rotation near the top of its trend channel with unfavorable near-term risk-reward, though the long-run outperformance trend is intact.
Positioning is neutral to underweight, the bar for growth is low, and ex-Tech earnings growth is forecast at 21% yoy. A rotation into them should ease breadth concerns.
Positioning fell to notably underweight (17th percentile) and the sector had its biggest fund outflows in seven months.
Low Tech exposure (9% versus 40% in the US and 30% in Asia) favors Europe if the rotation away from Tech continues.

earnings_insights: DB forecasts Q3 2026 Tech (MCG & Tech) earnings growth of about 55% yoy, an estimate for the quarter not yet reported.
DB forecasts Q3 2026 S&P 500 ex-Tech earnings growth of 21% yoy (estimate), versus 23% in Q2 2026 (reported), with the median S&P 500 company growing in the mid-teens (estimate).
DB S&P 500 forecasts: 2026 target 8000, 2026 EPS $358, 2027 EPS $420.
risk_factors: Tech rotation tops have historically reversed as inverted V-turns, with about 16pp of potential relative downside.
Concerns about future Tech profitability may cap the stock reaction to strong Q3 earnings.
A Tech reversal may be accompanied by a broader selloff if it coincides with an exogenous shock.
Vol control and systematic positioning is stretched, limiting further equity buying capacity.
Financials positioning is notably underweight and fund outflows are the largest in seven months.
charts_described: Figure 1: MCG & Tech ratio to the rest of the S&P 500 (log, reindexed) with a trend since 2016 growing 14.2% annualized and a band of +/-10%; prior rotation turning points marked on Mar 30, Oct 29, Jun 1, Dec 24, Apr 4, Jul 10, Apr 25, Sep 6 and Jul 29.

Table of rotations into Tech: the 5th rotation (Jul 29 to Oct 8, 2026, 52 trading days) returned MCG & Tech +15.1% versus ex-MCG & Tech -2.9%, 18.1pp relative, S&P 500 +6.1%, equal-weighted S&P 500 -1.7%.

Table of rotations away from Tech: median MCG & Tech -14.8% and -17.9pp relative; average -16.6% and -17.9pp relative; last one Jun 1 to Jul 29, 2026 was -11.8% (-18.4pp relative) over 43 trading days.
vol_and_positioning: Aggregate equity positioning 0.23sd (56th percentile); discretionary -0.23sd (32nd percentile); systematic 0.79sd (85th percentile); large caps 0.53sd (81st percentile); small caps -0.39sd (32nd percentile).
Vol control funds' equity allocation is at the 99th percentile (98th on the chart as of Oct 1) and their sensitivity to selloffs declined materially.
CTA equity positioning is at the 67th percentile: US 67th, Europe 76th, EM 75th, Japan 56th. Bond shorts are extreme and dollar longs are at the 97th percentile.
Risk parity equity allocation is at the 77th percentile, with US at the 84th percentile.

Call/put volume ratio (5d ma) is at the 80th percentile, total net call volume at the 99th percentile, and S&P 500 3m 90-110 skew rose. A basket of the highest net call volume stocks and a basket of the most shorted stocks both underperformed this week.
Equity L/S hedge fund beta to the S&P 500 is at the 90th percentile (1m) and 92nd percentile (3m).
Past rotations away from Tech lasted a median of about 43 to 109 trading days and averaged -16.6% for MCG & Tech and -17.9pp versus the rest.
Buyback announcements: $192bn weekly/3m reference on the buybacks tracker and $176bn for the sector announced buybacks over the last 3 months.
geopolitical: The start of the Iran war and Liberation Day are cited as large exogenous shocks that coincided with prior Tech rotations and dragged all stocks down.

tension_points.bull_case: Longer-run Tech outperformance remains intact at 14pp annually on much stronger earnings growth, with Q3 Tech earnings growth of about 55% yoy.
tension_points.bear_case: Risk-reward is unfavorable near term, with about 4pp of upside to the channel top versus potentially 16pp of relative downside, and profitability concerns that strong earnings may not resolve.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Tech's relative performance continuing above the top of its long-run trend channel (about 4pp above the current level) rather than turning at the edge as in prior rotations.

tension_points.bull_case: A rotation into other sectors and small caps should alleviate market breadth concerns, with ex-Tech growth at 21% yoy and a low bar.
tension_points.bear_case: Past rotations away from Tech have come with broader selloffs, though colored by exogenous shocks like Liberation Day and the start of the Iran war.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A rotation away from Tech that is not accompanied by a large exogenous shock would indicate a benign rotation rather than a broad selloff.
